target_customer: Real estate development professionals at launch (owners, builders, investors, brokers, local officials), later members and organizers of large online communities
problem: Real estate deal flow and community conversation were scattered across generic tools. Later the product became a messenger for large interest communities that wanted something between Telegram and a social network.
business_model: Free messenger with planned transaction tools for real estate deals (offers, escrow, signatures); no revenue model confirmed

founders.name: Yury Lifshits
founders.background_notes: Prior employer from the Crunchbase News round article. Education not found in an opened source.

founders.name: Steve Korshakov
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder with a Telegram engineering background in the Crunchbase News round article. The YC page lists only Lifshits.

exit.reason: The founder said in a Russian language interview that he had closed Openland; no date or detailed cause was given.

technical_complexity.rationale: A real time messenger with communities, roles and deal matching needs solid backend and mobile engineering, helped by a co-founder with Telegram engineering experience. Nothing research grade.

defensibility.rationale: Value would come from community density, but chat apps were easy to substitute and the product had no data or integration lock-in at launch.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large messengers already hosted communities. No incumbent copied Openland specifically; the company itself closed after a pivot to a general community messenger.

market_need_then: Real estate stakeholders relied on email and phone for deal matching, and communities of thousands were moving to chat apps. Demand evidence was thin: about 250 communities after a soft launch per a later launch thread.

branding.domain_note: Uses openland.com, the exact .com; how it was acquired is not stated in sources found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Warm, friendship focused positioning (make friends, safe self-expression, learn from others) per the YC description.

branding.community_and_virality: No evidence of memes, merch or fan accounts found. A founder interview and a Medium MVP review exist.

brand_strength.rationale: Little press about the brand itself; the name is generic and the audience small.

pivots.from: Messenger for real estate development professionals
pivots.why: Sources found say the team pivoted shortly after YC and rebuilt the messenger for communities; the stated reason was not found.

outcome_analysis: Openland raised a 2.25 million dollar seed after Winter 2018 as a real estate messenger, then pivoted to a general community messenger and reached only a few hundred communities. The founder later said he closed it. The exact cause is not public, so the failure factors are inferred from the pivot and modest community growth and should be read as tentative.
notes: Seed amount rests on Crunchbase News (which corrected an earlier 2.5M headline) and FinSMEs and CB Insights both report 2.25M. The second outlet snippets were seen in search results only. No competitors with sources dated near August 2018 were found; Slack, Discord and Telegram positioning appears only in a later launch thread. The openland.com page shows only a name and contact email.
